extracted.intended_audience: legislators, administrators, administrative tribunal members, and administrative law scholars concerned with social security appeals in Canada
extracted.subtask_short: administrative procedure for social security appeals
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive and prescriptive framework for the procedure of administrative appeal tribunals (especially the Pension Appeals Board) in social security matters, covering sources of procedure, stages from initial administrative decision to appeal and enforcement, and principles for reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of the administrative process
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules governing the initiation of the administrative process, whether begun by the administered subject or by the administering authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers how a case or application is started and the formalities required at the outset; the study treats initiation as the first phase to be regulated and described in any administrative-procedure framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathering of information required for a decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural standards for how administrative authorities gather the information necessary to reach a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes documentary procedures, medical or technical assessments, access to files, and the responsibilities of officials to collect accurate information for decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation in the decision-making process
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules enabling affected persons to take part in decisions that concern them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses rights to be heard, interventions, representation, and other participatory mechanisms described throughout the hearing and appeal stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms of consultation, notice and prior rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for consultation with affected parties, giving notice of proposed measures, and opportunities for prior correction or rectification before a decision is finalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes procedural steps that allow correction of errors and early resolution; these mechanisms reduce unfair surprise and promote substantive fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification, communication and publication of the decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations on administrative authorities to justify their decisions, communicate them to affected persons, and, where appropriate, publish decisions or reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on form letters, explanation of precedents in communications, and making reasons available to the public and to claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating of the decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural provisions allowing decisions to be updated or revised in light of new information or changes in circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers mechanisms such as reconsideration, review committees, or ministerial determinations to modify decisions post-issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avenues of recourse against the decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal channels by which decisions may be challenged, whether before the same authority, a higher administrative authority, an appeal tribunal, or the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies stages such as internal review, appeals to Minister, appeal to Pension Appeals Board, appeals to Review Committees/Umpire, and judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution of the decision by the administrative authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural obligations and methods for putting an administrative decision into effect once it has become final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes how benefits are paid or revoked, administrative follow-through, and communication to enforcement units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms of verification following the decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for post-decision verification, audits, and checks to ensure correct application and compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes benefit control, recovery of overpayments, statistical monitoring, and other verification steps described in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions applicable for failure to carry out the decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of sanctions (criminal or administrative) where obligations arising from decisions are not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiates criminal sanctions and administrative sanctions and discusses appropriate use and scope in social security context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities and time-frames
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal procedural requirements and statutory or regulatory time-limits that apply at various phases of the administrative process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes filing deadlines, extension of time limits, leave to appeal rules, timing for hearings, and statutory limitation periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between general and particular administrative decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that modes of procedure differ depending on whether a decision is general (regulatory) or particular (individual benefit/grant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides which procedural protections and steps are appropriate to each type of decision; the study stresses tailoring procedure to the nature of the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of administrative procedure — Legislation and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation and regulations as a primary source of procedural standards, either dispersed across statutes or organized in a general code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes two legislative models: dispersed procedural prescriptions (prevailing in Canada) and consolidated procedural codes (as in the U.S. and some provinces); deficiencies in texts lead to judicial interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of administrative procedure — Internal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal rules (minutes, policy statements, circulars, directives, manuals) as a source of day-to-day procedural practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules provide operational detail but are often not publicly known; they must be compatible with legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of administrative procedure — Customs and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Customs and established practices of administrative authorities as an informal source of procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though changeable over time and location, customs significantly affect practical procedure and should be considered in reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave to appeal and time-limit extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules governing when leave to appeal is required and the criteria for extending statutory time limits for appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study details differences across CPP benefits, QPP benefits, and unemployment insurance; guidance includes grounds and practice on granting leave or extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for the form and substance of a notice of appeal to an appeal tribunal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what must be included to constitute a valid notice of appeal and how withdrawal of appeals is handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-hearing preparations and incidental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for interventions, replies to notices of appeal, settlement before hearing, other incidents, and determination of time and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses how parties prepare files, file interventions, attempt settlements, and how the tribunal schedules and organizes hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of the hearing (participants and examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on who may participate in hearings and the manner in which the appeal is examined at the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers participation by parties and representatives, examination and cross-examination practices, evidence presentation, and special procedures for different types of pensions (disability, survivor's, retirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rendering the decision (form, reasons and statistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural standards for how the tribunal renders decisions, provides reasons, and records statistical outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes timing for decisions, the form of reasons, publication or circulation of decisions, and collection of statistics on outcomes and processing times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal control over decisions and internal review
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms for administrative authorities to exercise internal control and to conduct internal reviews of decisions prior to external appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes internal review units, reconsideration procedures (e.g., QPP reconsideration committee), and the role of central units in quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAB and judicial review (control and finality)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relationship between the Pension Appeals Board's decisions and judicial review by courts; scope and limits of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats PAB as often a court of last resort in administrative process and discusses standards of review, availability of judicial intervention, and how PAB decisions are subject to or insulated from review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing the public — access to legal rules and caselaw
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation to provide public access to the Act, regulations and relevant caselaw so members of the public can know the legal rules affecting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include publishing statutes/regulations, making caselaw accessible, and including precedential explanations in communications (e.g., form letters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding procedure — contact with officials, form letters, access to the file
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical measures to help applicants understand and navigate procedure, including accessible contact points, standardized correspondence, and rights to inspect their files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study recommends clear form letters, proactive contact with officials, and easier file access to enhance informed participation and reduce misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing the decision-maker — contact with applicant and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural duties to ensure decision-makers are adequately informed through direct contact with applicants and proper documentation submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages mechanisms to surface relevant evidence to decision-makers and standards for documentation completeness and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic objectives of administrative procedure — requirements of the public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative procedure must reconcile efficient public administration with the public interest in effective decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study frames public-interest requirements as one of the central objectives that procedure must serve alongside individual safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic objectives of administrative procedure — safeguards for individual interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative procedure must include protections for individual rights and legitimate private interests affected by administrative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguards include notice, participation, access to reasons, avenues of recourse, and procedural transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of administrative efficiency — possession of exact information by the decision-maker
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-making efficiency depends on the decision-maker having precise and accurate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes investigative functions, proper documentation, and organizational arrangements to ensure information accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of administrative efficiency — speed in decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness is a core procedural objective: decisions should be made promptly to serve administrative efficiency and fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study examines average processing times, backlogs, and recommends measures to improve speed without compromising fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of administrative efficiency — existence of guarantees that decisions will be executed
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative efficiency requires mechanisms ensuring that decisions, once taken, will actually be executed and enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedures for recovery of overpayments, enforcement mechanisms, and institutional guarantees to secure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reorganization of review and redress (structural remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional reforms such as reorganizing pre-contentious review, abolishing lower appeal authorities, and reorganizing higher appeal authority to improve procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study proposes structural changes (e.g., abolition or consolidation of appeal steps) to simplify and improve redress mechanisms in social security litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcing decisions — recovery of overpayments
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and legal measures for recovering benefits paid in error or overpaid to beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses statutory bases, fairness considerations (intent vs. error), and administrative practices for repayment and collection.
